findings.label: M-01
findings.title: A THIRD PARTY can sandwich another staker's autoAnnihilate and be paid out of freshly minted unbacked phUSD, bounded only by a cross-repo parameter StableStakerV2 never reads
findings.description: A third party -- not the caller -- can sandwich any staker's autoAnnihilate against the AMM-backed ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy and be paid out of freshly minted, unbacked phUSD. The sole bound on the induced shortfall is slippageToleranceBps, which lives in reflax-yield-vault, is documented THERE as a DEPOSIT haircut control, and is never read, bounded, asserted or reported by StableStakerV2. LAW-3 OWNER FOOTGUN: a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised that a deposit-side knob in a different repository is the only cap on this contract's unbacked-phUSD inflation. Surprise => footgun => in scope.
findings.impact: Protocol value leak via unbacked phUSD inflation. Marginal dilution is 1x (s*N) on the COLLATERAL removed, NOT the 2x phUSDMinted line item -- half the top-up substitutes for phUSD Antimatter would have minted anyway (Antimatter.sol:263). Extractable slack is N*(s-d-f) because the strategy's minOut floor anchors to vault NAV rather than market price (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:166-168). The attack is NEGATIVE-SUM -- the protocol loses more than the attacker gains -- which is an argument about the attacker's incentive and is NEVER a reason to downgrade the protocol's loss.
findings.lossSizingRule: Size the loss on the COLLATERAL REMOVED (~1x the induced shortfall). Do NOT headline phUSDMinted (a 2x overstatement) and do NOT use the totalSupply delta (it reads zero).
findings.severityBasis: C4 Medium: no direct theft of a user's assets, but a protocol value leak with stated assumptions and an external requirement (an AMM-backed ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy). Severity FINALISED at Medium by the severity-classifier on the delivered fork PoC; the run-time provisional caveat is discharged. POST-REVIEW 2026-09-01: severity RE-CONFIRMED at Medium and recorded at the UPPER END of Medium on new configuration evidence. See `postReviewEvidence`. The new evidence does NOT move the finding toward High.
attackPath: Victim (or any steered staker) submits autoAnnihilate.
Attacker front-runs, moving the AMM price against the strategy's exit.
autoAnnihilate exits into the moved market; the realised shortfall is bounded only by slippageToleranceBps, set in reflax-yield-vault.
The shortfall is made whole by _annihilateAndTopUp minting phUSD directly against FlaxToken (see L-01 -- no cap, no collateral).
Attacker back-runs, capturing N*(s-d-f); the protocol carries ~1x the induced shortfall as unbacked phUSD.
findings.recommendation: Bound and assert slippageToleranceBps from StableStakerV2's side (or read and report it), and document its dual role. Do not rely on the sibling repo's deposit-side documentation as the cap on this contract's inflation.
findings.knownIssueRuling: NOT SUPPRESSED. N28 authorises the MECHANISM and rounding direction only and expressly says nothing about backing, the size/unboundedness of the inflation, or the interaction with N20's now-larger accepted extraction. N20 covers the SELF-sandwich only. C8 is registry-only with authority NONE and may not suppress a Law-3 footgun. Project memory 'V2 emits Antimatter, premise VOID': V2's Antimatter is redeemable into UNBACKED phUSD, so the minter-cushion / opportunity-cost suppressions are DEAD for V2.

postReviewEvidence.MARGIN_DIRECTION_CORRECTED: DIRECTION CORRECTION -- SUPERSEDES AN EARLIER WORDING. An earlier framing said the live 120bps sits 'inside the unpriced-capital-cost margin', implying a THIN margin. THAT HAD THE DIRECTION BACKWARDS and must not be recorded that way. Unpriced flash-loan, inventory and MEV-bribe costs push TRUE breakeven UP -- i.e. FURTHER ABOVE 142bps and further AWAY from 120 -- so the real margin at the live setting is WIDER than the nominal 22bps, not narrower. CORRECT FRAMING: the deployed 120bps sits at ~85% of the NOMINAL 142bps breakeven (where the 50bps NatSpec example implied 35%), so the comfort margin is roughly HALVED IN NOMINAL TERMS -- but NO profitable attack is demonstrated at any configured value, and this evidence does NOT move the finding toward High.
postReviewEvidence.FOOTGUN_STRONGEST_FORM: THE OPERATING BAND IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ACROSS THE MAINNET FLEET. Four mainnet-facing artifacts carry FOUR DIFFERENT VALUES (30 / 100 / 120 / 150) for ONE parameter on ONE asset -- and the artifact with the LOOSEST value (DeployUSDeMarketYieldStrategy.s.sol, 120bps, --broadcast --ledger) is the one with NO preflight guard, sitting ABOVE the <=100bps ceiling its sibling script MigrateStableStakerMainnet.s.sol:312 enforces for the SAME asset over the SAME Curve pair. The ONLY code bound anywhere is require(_bps <= MAX_BPS) at reflax-yield-vault/src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:88-89, i.e. 100%. OPERATIONAL DISCIPLINE IS DEMONSTRABLY NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE MISSING CODE BOUND. This is the sharpest form of the Law-3 argument: the owner is already operating near a line nothing in StableStakerV2 discloses, bounds or reports, and the fleet does not agree with itself about where that line is.
postReviewEvidence.RECOMMENDATION_URGENCY: This makes M-01's recommended LOCAL maxShortfallBps invariant materially MORE URGENT: it is the one bound that no cross-repo script drift can silently widen.
postReviewEvidence.GRIEFER_NOTE: THE PROTOCOL'S LOSS IS NOT GATED ON ATTACKER PROFITABILITY. The attack is NEGATIVE-SUM, so a griefer, a competitor, or anyone holding an offsetting phUSD short incurs the protocol's FULL loss at ANY tolerance -- INCLUDING 50bps. 142bps is the threshold for an UNSUBSIDISED attack, not the threshold for HARM.

findings.label: M-02
findings.title: autoAnnihilate -- the REWARD path every staker is steered into -- consumes the shared underwater-WITHDRAWAL buffer, and can deny another staker a solvent exit
findings.description: The buffer exists to let underwater WITHDRAWALS be paid at par. autoAnnihilate, the reward path stakers are steered into while claimEnabled is false, draws from that same shared buffer. One staker harvesting rewards can therefore exhaust the buffer and deny a different, solvent staker their exit.
findings.impact: C4 Medium: assets are not directly stolen, but protocol function/availability is impacted -- a solvent user's withdraw() reverts because a DIFFERENT user harvested rewards.
findings.severityBasis: C4 LOW. Originally filed Medium (availability) by the severity-classifier; OVERTURNED to Low by the severity-auditor on 2026-09-01 and adjudicated ACCEPTED by the coordinator. See `severityChange` for the full basis -- the asymmetry claim is falsified by the source and the PoC's control is wrong. The PoC still passes; what it proves is narrower than the headline.
attackPath: Alice calls autoAnnihilate (the reward path; claim() is shut with claimEnabled false).
Her reward draw consumes the shared underwater-withdrawal buffer.
Bob's solvent withdraw() reverts 'StableStaker: strategy underwater'.
Counterfactually (without Alice's harvest) Bob's withdraw succeeds at par.
findings.recommendation: Do not let the reward path consume the withdraw buffer, or gate autoAnnihilate on !_isUnderwater.

poc.observation: Bob's withdraw reverts 'StableStaker: strategy underwater' after Alice's autoAnnihilate; counterfactually it succeeds at par.
poc.controlGap: PoC_ss18m2_BufferSpend.t.sol's counterfactual is 'buffer intact vs Alice's autoAnnihilate'. The CORRECT control is 'Alice's withdraw(dai, 50 ether) vs Alice's autoAnnihilate(dai)'. In the PoC's own setup an equivalent withdraw routes the identical underwater branch, draws the identical 50e18 and denies Bob identically. Bob is therefore NOT an incremental victim against the correct baseline -- which is exactly the premise the re-file basis claimed to falsify in wont-fix 69c7666e. RE-FILE BASIS #2 DOES NOT SURVIVE.

findings.knownIssueRuling: THE CLAUDE.md UNDERWATER CARVE-OUT SUPPRESSES NOTHING; THE MECHANISM SURVIVES IN FULL. The carve-out at CLAUDE.md:216-221 is the tail of known-issue N19, and the run-18 KI re-extraction rules N19's authority explicitly and twice: 'N19 - caveat STANDS, no suppression authority ... N19 evidences intent and nothing more', and sanitizer usage rule 3 'N19 suppresses nothing (unanchored self-citation)'. priorArtDisclosure.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
priorArtDisclosure.triageReasonQuotedVerbatim: Intended design (confirmed by protocol owner). The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution. The report itself concedes there is no incremental victim (the slow staker is baseline-unchanged vs a no-buffer world).
priorArtDisclosure.relation: SAME CLASS (FCFS buffer consumption), DIFFERENT FINDING on new story-027/028 code.
priorArtDisclosure.reFileBasis: RE-FILED AGAINST A WONT-FIX, DISCLOSED NOT SILENTLY OVERRIDDEN. TWO of that wont-fix's own premises are FALSIFIED at cf8de27: (1) it sized the buffer against daily-volume WITHDRAWALS -- the buffer is now also consumed by the REWARD path, which was not in the sizing input; and (2) it rested on 'no incremental victim' -- Bob's exit is now DENIED by Alice's REWARD harvest, which is precisely an incremental victim. The owner may still wont-fix it; the basis is on the record either way.
priorArtDisclosure.reFileBasisAmended_2026-09-01: RE-FILE BASIS #2 DOES NOT SURVIVE. The 'incremental victim' premise is REINSTATED, not falsified: against the correct control (an equivalent-size withdraw by the same caller) Bob is denied identically, so Alice's autoAnnihilate creates no incremental victim. Basis #1 survives only PARTIALLY, as a RATE argument (while claimEnabled is false a reward-only staker is FORCED into a principal exit that draws the buffer), with an UNCHANGED CEILING. 69c7666e's wont-fix status is NOT changed by this run and never was.

severityChange.basisVerbatim: M-02's load-bearing asymmetry claim is FALSIFIED BY THE SOURCE. It argued `withdraw` consumes the buffer 1:1 with a position LEAVING while `autoAnnihilate` is a repeatable reward action whose caller keeps their position. But autoAnnihilate debits principal identically at StableStakerV2.sol:554-560 -- `gross = netWanted > user.amount ? user.amount : netWanted; user.amount -= gross; pool.totalStaked -= gross;` -- so every call burns principal 1:1 exactly as withdraw does, and netWanted = min(owed, user.amount*scale)/scale caps the draw at the caller's own principal, making autoAnnihilate a STRICTLY NARROWER buffer consumer than a same-size withdraw.
severityChange.basisIndependentlyVerified: The finding-manager re-read src/StableStakerV2.sol:550-565 at cf8de27 before applying: the cited debit triple (`gross = netWanted > user.amount ? user.amount : netWanted;` then `user.amount -= gross; pool.totalStaked -= gross;`) is present as quoted, and the in-source comment states netWanted is ALREADY capped at the caller's principal, so the second clamp is belt-and-braces. The overturn's load-bearing citation reproduces.
severityChange.pocControlGap: PoC_ss18m2_BufferSpend.t.sol's counterfactual is 'buffer intact vs Alice's autoAnnihilate'. The CORRECT control is 'Alice's withdraw(dai, 50 ether) vs Alice's autoAnnihilate(dai)'. In the PoC's own setup an equivalent withdraw routes the identical underwater branch, draws the identical 50e18 and denies Bob identically. Bob is therefore NOT an incremental victim against the correct baseline -- which is exactly the premise the re-file basis claimed to falsify in wont-fix 69c7666e. RE-FILE BASIS #2 DOES NOT SURVIVE.
severityChange.whatSurvivesAtLow: Re-file basis #1, PARTIAL. 69c7666e sized the buffer against WITHDRAWAL demand, and while claimEnabled is false a staker who wants only their reward is FORCED into a principal exit that draws the buffer. That shifts the RATE of buffer consumption above what voluntary-exit demand predicts. It is a likelihood argument on an already-accepted mechanism with an UNCHANGED CEILING.

findings.description: _phUSD().mint(address(this), phUSDMinted) at :646 is gated only by canMint + mintVersion (phUSDMintAvailable) -- no cap, no allowance, no collateral. The route, not the value, decides the outcome.

findings.title: The internally-computed minPhUSDOut is TAUTOLOGICAL and cannot bind: totalPhUSD == minPhUSDOut identically, zero margin
findings.description: _annihilateMeasured passes annihilatable + calculateMintAmount(token, netUsed); Antimatter checks totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable against it, and mintedForStable IS exactly calculateMintAmount with no fee and no partial fill (PhusdStableMinter.sol:212,232). Neither hazard the NatSpec names is catchable: rate movement between quote and burn cannot occur because the quote is evaluated in the ARGUMENT EXPRESSION of the guarded call, so there is no window; and a mint cap biting REVERTS rather than under-delivering, so a floor never sees it.
findings.impact: A guard that reads as protection but is provably inert. QA/Low.
findings.severityBasis: C4 Low: spec deviation / dead guard, no value at risk.
findings.recommendation: Either give the floor real margin from an independent quote source, or delete it and correct the NatSpec that claims it protects against rate movement and a mint cap.
findings.knownIssueRuling: NOT SUPPRESSED, and note the DIRECTION: N32 is the item that ASSERTS this floor is 'the only in-path guard against the exchange rate moving or a mint cap biting between quote and burn'. A known issue cannot suppress the finding that refutes its own stated rationale.

findings.label: L-03
findings.title: Sub-unit backlog is unreachable once emissions stop: 0 < owed < scale with non-zero principal reverts 'nothing to annihilate', and no other reward path is open
findings.description: netWanted == 0 and excess == 0, so the require at :545 reverts. With antimatterPerDay at 0 the backlog can never grow past `scale`, and with claimEnabled false claim() is shut, so the user has NO reward path: claim shut, autoAnnihilate reverts, and emergencyWithdraw zeroes the backlog at :702 (N4).
findings.impact: Liveness failure for a bounded amount. Bounded by `scale`, hence Low.
findings.severityBasis: C4 Low: reward-path liveness, value bounded by one `scale` unit.
findings.recommendation: Allow a sub-unit backlog to be swept, or fold it forward rather than reverting.

findings.label: F-04
findings.title: The autoAnnihilate NatSpec states the buffer invariant UNQUALIFIED -- 'the invariant that autoAnnihilate never spends a unit of it survives intact' -- which the underwater path falsifies
findings.description: CLAUDE.md at least qualifies the claim ('a statement about the normal path, not an invariant of every call'). The contract source does not, and adds 'No other staker's position is touched by one caller's exit haircut' -- which the M-02 PoC falsifies directly. The contract is the artifact an integrator reads. Per standing project memory, a falsely-exhaustive doc raises severity rather than sanitizing the defect.
findings.impact: An integrator reading the contract is told an invariant holds that does not. Low.
findings.severityBasis: C4 Low, faithfulness:true. Routed to spec-conformance.md, NOT the QA bundle's code section.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the comment at :484-488 to the normal (non-underwater) path, and delete or qualify the 'no other staker's position is touched' sentence.
findings.independenceRuling: LANDS INDEPENDENTLY OF M-02's DISPOSITION. Split out of M-02 and kept separate: the code fix (do not let the reward path consume the withdraw buffer, or gate autoAnnihilate on !_isUnderwater) and the doc fix (qualify :484-488) are independent and land separately. If a human wont-fixes M-02 on intent, THIS ONE STILL HAS TO LAND -- indeed a wont-fix on intent makes the unqualified comment MORE wrong, not less.
findings.primarySurvivingArtifact: PRIMARY SURVIVING ARTIFACT OF THIS LINE (recorded 2026-09-01). With M-02 / ss18m2 lowered to Low by the post-review severity overturn, F-04 is now the PRIMARY surviving artifact of the autoAnnihilate/buffer line. It LANDS INDEPENDENTLY of M-02's disposition: the :484-488 text is FALSE AS WRITTEN on the underwater branch regardless of how M-02 resolves. DO NOT let F-04 be swept up in the M-02 downgrade, and do not lower or retire it on the strength of that downgrade.

findings.label: F-01
findings.title: Law-2 story-unsafe escalation: stories 026/027/028 model ONLY the self-sandwich; the third-party sandwicher is never considered, and the make-whole guarantee removes the victim's defensive incentive
findings.description: The stories' accepted-extraction reasoning is 'bounded by the caller's own stake and accrued antimatter ... Human decision: accepted' -- a bound that exists ONLY for a self-sandwicher. A third party is bounded by the VICTIM's stake, which the accepting human never priced. story-028 additionally deleted the caller's minPhUSDOut knob (N32), removing the last caller-side lever. CLAUDE.md:235-236 -- 'Ordinary sandwiching of the exit is not new: a plain withdraw sells into the same AMM with the same protection' -- is materially wrong on the economics: under a plain withdraw the sandwich victim bears their own loss and therefore has a defensive incentive, whereas the make-whole top-up transfers the loss to the protocol and removes it.
findings.impact: LAW 2. Not tallied in the H/M count. The decision record accepted an extraction bound that does not hold for the actor who matters.
findings.severityBasis: Law-2 faithfulness item. NOT severity-bearing; must never enter the H/M tally.
findings.recommendation: Amend the story/decision record to price the third-party sandwicher, and correct CLAUDE.md:235-236's economics claim.
findings.citationDiscipline: The security narrative is stated ONCE, in M-01. F-01 CITES it rather than restating it. Different channel (spec-conformance.md, explicitly NOT the QA bundle), different law (Law 2 vs Law 1), different remedy (amend the story + correct CLAUDE.md vs. bound the parameter).

findings.label: Q-01
findings.title: The `gross` clamp is provably redundant but fails SILENTLY rather than loudly; a future refactor that breaks its premise mints free phUSD instead of reverting
findings.description: capped <= user.amount * scale implies gross == netWanted always. But netUsed clamps against netWanted and the frictionless target is sized on netWanted, so if the premise ever breaks the contract pays a target it did not debit for -- free phUSD -- rather than reverting. The comment's own justification ('the debit below underflows if it is ever wrong') is backwards: the debit uses `gross`, which is the clamped value, so it cannot underflow.
findings.impact: Latent: correct today, silently wrong under a future refactor. QA.
findings.severityBasis: QA. No value at risk at HEAD.
findings.recommendation: require(gross == netWanted) so the premise fails loudly.
